B. Is this measure already running in South Karelia wellbeing services county (or in the HUS university hospital area that treats its patients)?
A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Travel and accommodation support for patients far from the university hospital. Patients who must travel for surgery or weeks of radiotherapy get a booked patient hotel, organised transport and a named contact, so that distance is not the reason to choose a non-curative treatment.
effect_summary_en: The English registry study (Crawford 2009, 34,923 patients) links the longest travel time to lower odds of lung cancer surgery (OR 0.60, combined with deprivation), but it did not test any travel support service.
supported_en: A northern England registry study (Br J Cancer 2009) found that the most deprived patients living furthest away had odds of surgery of 0.60 compared with the least deprived living nearest.
not_supported_en: No study we read shows that travel or hotel support raises the curative-treatment share, or by how many percentage points (our assumption is 1.0).
in_use_quote: Hotellihuonevaraukset tekee hoitava yksikkö. Potilashotelli sijaitsee Scandic Meilahti -hotellissa Helsingissä.
missing_en: No page we read shows organised transport or a named contact for South Karelia patients travelling to HUS.
summary_en: HUS says on its own site that it runs a patient hotel at Scandic Meilahti in Helsinki for patients whose treatment lasts more than a day, and that the treating unit books the rooms. No page we read shows organised transport or a named contact for South Karelia patients. On effect, a 2009 English registry study links longer travel time to lower odds of surgery (OR 0.60), but it did not test a support service, so our assumed gain of 1 percentage point has no direct evidence behind it.
unanswered_en: We did not search or read Ekhva pages on organised transport or a contact person for treatment at HUS, or any study that tests travel support itself.
